newsitem.title: UK: Britain's Clarke says recovery best for generation.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Clarke says recovery best for generation.

text.p: Britain is enjoying its brightest economic prospects for a generation with a balanced and sustainable recovery, Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke said on Monday.

In a text prepared for delivery to an annual conference, he said: "Of course regional differences remain, whether because of history, geography or industrial structure. But each and every region of the United Kingdom is benefiting from this recovery.
"We have never faced such good economic prospects in the memory of most people."
Clarke told the Newspaper Conference in London that unemployment would have to fall much more before labour shortages started to put upward pressure on wages and prices.

Similarly, while regional skill shortages can put upward pressure on inflation, the more balanced nature of the current recovery means the economy can sustain higher levels of activity without running into inflationary pressure, he added.

"This government's record on inflation is the best for nearly 50 years. Our proven determination to keep inflation low is helping keep this recovery on track. There are clear signs that the inflation culture that brought every previous recovery to a premature halt has been broken," he said.
All serious economic commentators agreed that on present policies, growth will be sustained this year and into next year.

"The United Kingdom is approaching its sixth year of healthy growth...GDP is rising in each and every region of the UK. And what is more, growth in this recovery has been better balanced across the regions than at the same stage of the previous recovery."

Clarke said he believed the outcome of the forthcoming British general election -- which must be held before May 22 -- would be decided on the core issues of jobs, living standards and the health of the British economy.
